page: Microsoft Azure F16-4ams_v7 is an x86_64 virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor operating at up to 4.5 GHz under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is provisioned with 4 dedicated physical cores without simultaneous multithreading, providing 4 dedicated vCPUs. It features a substantial memory footprint of 128.0 GB, which equals 32.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The processor architecture includes 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, alongside support for advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 (f, vnni, and bf16), AES, VAES, and SHA_NI.

This instance configuration contains no local storage and does not incorporate discrete GPU accelerators. Host storage tasks and persistent state rely entirely on remote network storage interfaces, with support for Premium Storage tiers. Because the instance restricts active compute to 4 vCPUs while retaining a 128.0 GB RAM allocation, it addresses memory-constrained workloads without incurring the overhead of additional vCPUs. This constrained-core design provides qualitative cost advantages for software environments that license per physical core or per vCPU.

Benchmark evaluations reveal top-tier single-core CPU throughput, as reflected in stress-ng single-core tests and single-threaded gzip and bzip3 operations. Multi-core performance metrics, such as PassMark CPU and multi-threaded decompression, place in the middle tier, corresponding to the 4-core physical count. Memory throughput registers at 55.23 GB/s for uncached reads and 34.62 GB/s for uncached writes. The F16-4ams_v7 is suitable for core-licensed relational database engines, Redis or in-memory caching architectures, and memory-intensive single-threaded execution tasks.
description: Microsoft Azure F16-4ams_v7 is a memory-dense virtual machine configured with 4 dedicated physical cores (4 vCPUs) on an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor running at 4.5 GHz. The configuration allocates 128.0 GB of memory, equating to 32.0 GB per core, making it well positioned for memory-heavy computing with reduced core counts. The processor incorporates 32 MB of L3 cache and supports AVX-512 instruction extensions. No local storage or discrete GPU accelerators are bundled, requiring network-attached storage for persistent disks. Benchmark results demonstrate top-tier single-core compute and data compression throughput, while multi-threaded compute and uncached memory bandwidth align within average ranges due to the four-core limitation. This profile provides a cost-efficient hardware setup for software where licensing costs scale per core, making the instance suitable for in-memory databases, key-value stores, and analytics jobs with high memory requirements.
